headline: Ho'nble Union Minister for Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying & Panchayatiraj Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh launched Live Stock insurance portal
fullText:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

Ho'nble Union Minister for Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying & Panchayatiraj Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh launched Live Stock insurance portal

The digital platform aimed at transforming livestock insurance delivery across the country under the Livestock Insurance activity of National Livestock Mission (NLM)

Ho'nble Union MoS for Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying & Panchayatiraj Prof S P Singh Baghel was also present on the occasion

28 SEP 2026 9:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, today launched the Livestock Insurance Portal (https://rashtriyapashubima.dahd.gov.in), a comprehensive digital platform aimed at transforming livestock insurance delivery across the country under the Livestock Insurance activity of National Livestock Mission (NLM).

The Portal was launched by Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Hon'ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, in presence of Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel, Hon'ble Minister of State of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary, Animal Husbandry and Dairyingand other senior officials of the Department, representatives of State Governments, insurance companies and sectoral stakeholders. Besides, more than 4,000 participants joined online.

While highlighting the contours of scheme, premium rates, contribution of the farmer & other aspects of scheme on the Livestock Insurance activity, Shri Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary (AHD) informed that more than 30 lakh animals have already been insured during the year.

Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel, Hon'ble Minister of State of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying expressed concern over uncertainty of agriculture and expressed hope that the livestock insurance portal will be a great relief to the farmers.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Hon'ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, highlighted that livestock serves as a critical source of income and livelihood for millions of rural households. He emphasized that timely and affordable insurance protection safeguards farmers against financial losses arising from mortality, disease outbreaks, accidents, natural calamities and other unforeseen risks. He stressed upon the measures for awareness programmes for the farmers, to provide them maximum benefit under the scheme. He also urged the Insurance Companies, State Governments and other stakeholders to give wider publicity to the scheme through their respective social media and IEC campaigns.

The newly launched Livestock Insurance Portal provides an end-to-end digital ecosystem for policy issuance, premium management, claim processing, beneficiary verification and real-time monitoring. The platform brings together farmers, State Governments, Insurance Companies and implementing agencies on a single transparent and technology-enabled interface.

The Portal is expected to:

simplify and expedite livestock insurance enrolment

enhance transparency and accountability in claim settlement

enable real-time tracking and monitoring of policies

improve accessibility and ease of doing business for farmers and insurance providers

strengthen data-driven decision-making for effective scheme implementation.

The initiative marks a significant step towards digital transformation in the livestock sector and supports the Government's vision of leveraging technology for farmer welfare and rural prosperity.

headline: Rashtriya Raksha University to Launch Second Batch of Masters in Financial and Economic Security
fullText:
Ministry of Home Affairs

Rashtriya Raksha University to Launch Second Batch of Masters in Financial and Economic Security

28 SEP 2026 8:44PM by PIB Mumbai

Mumbai, 28 September 2026

Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, with the Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, is set to launch the second batch of its Masters in Financial and Economic Security (MFES) program in November 2026. The program follows the successful completion of its first cohort, which comprised more than 40 professionals from diverse fields, including banking, law enforcement, investigation, academia, entrepreneurship and legal services.

Designed especially for working professionals, the one-year program is offered in a hybrid mode, enabling participants to continue their professional responsibilities while gaining specialised knowledge and practical skills. The program places strong emphasis on practical learning, hands-on training and exposure to contemporary challenges in financial and economic security.

Building Capacity for Emerging Financial and Economic Threats

Financial security and economic integrity are increasingly important in an interconnected global economy. The rapid evolution of financial technologies, digital assets and cross-border financial activities has also created new avenues for financial crime and economic disruption. There is therefore a growing need to build a specialised cadre of professionals capable of understanding, preventing and responding to emerging financial and economic crimes, thereby strengthening India’s economic resilience and contributing to international peace, stability and security.

Speaking at the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Mumbai, Mr. Sunil Kavishwar, Director, School of Criminal Law and Military Law, RRU highlighted the growing importance of safeguarding the integrity and resilience of financial systems. He noted that financial crimes are continuously evolving, moving beyond traditional forms into emerging areas such as virtual digital assets, terror financing, proliferation financing, and technology-enabled financial crimes. The increasing use of sophisticated technologies by criminal networks has further created new challenges for enforcement, regulatory and financial institutions.

Mr. Kavishwar highlighted that RRU has taken the lead in developing a global platform for capacity building, specialised training and knowledge exchange in the emerging field of financial and economic security. The University is working towards bringing together professionals, experts and institutions from across relevant domains to strengthen specialised understanding and practical capabilities in this area. He further highlighted that the MFES program brings together not only academicians but also experienced practitioners and working professionals who bring direct expertise from the field and will contribute to the program as faculty and resource persons.

Mr. Harshit Singh, Teaching Cum Research Officer, RRU spoke about the importance of developing a specialised professional cadre equipped to address emerging financial and economic security challenges. He emphasised that such trained professionals can contribute to strengthening India’s economic resilience, supporting sustainable national growth and enhancing the country’s contribution to global financial security and stability.

The program also aligns with the broader vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s Viksit Bharat @2047, by contributing to the development of skilled professionals capable of protecting financial systems, strengthening institutional capacity and responding effectively to emerging economic and security threats. As India’s economy becomes increasingly integrated with global financial systems, such specialised expertise can play an important role in supporting secure, resilient and sustainable growth.

The second cohort is open to national and international participants, providing an opportunity for professionals from different jurisdictions and sectors to learn and engage with contemporary issues of financial and economic security. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) is also a Knowledge Partner in the program.

Interested professionals can register through the official Rashtriya Raksha University admission portal. The program is intended to provide participants with a multidisciplinary understanding of financial and economic security through academic instruction, practical exposure and interaction with experts from the field.

For further information and registration, visit the official Rashtriya Raksha University website.

headline: India showcases Forest and Landscape Restoration Initiatives at COFO 28, in Rome
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

India showcases Forest and Landscape Restoration Initiatives at COFO 28, in Rome

International Cooperation must support Country-driven Implementation, Capacity Development, Technology Transfer and Measurable Outcomes on Ground: India

28 SEP 2026 8:21PM by PIB Delhi

India highlighted its significant achievement in forest and landscape restoration and reaffirmed its commitment to sustainable forest management, climate action and resilient forest landscapes at the Twenty-eighth Session of the FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization) Committee on Forestry (COFO 28), being held in Rome from 28th September to 2nd October 2026. Delivering its Statement during COFO 28, India welcomed FAO’s focus on Forest and Landscape Restoration, and emphasised that sustainable forest management provides an integrated framework for addressing restoration at the landscape level while responding to national circumstances and the needs of local communities.

India highlighted the consistent progress made in enhancing its forest resources. The country’s forest and tree cover stands at 82.74 million hectares, constituting 25.17% of its geographical area. The FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment 2025 ranks India 9th globally in forest area and 3rd in net annual forest area gain. Forests and trees also remain central to India’s climate commitments. India has created an additional carbon sink of 2.29 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent by 2021 and has enhanced its ambition to create an additional carbon sink of 3.5–4.0 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent by 2035, compared with 2005 levels.

The Statement further highlighted its commitment under the Bonn Challenge to restore 26 million hectares of degraded and deforested land by 2030, of which 21.76 million hectares have already been brought under restoration. Further, major landscape restoration initiatives being undertaken were showcased. Under the Aravalli Green Wall, approximately 6.45 million hectares of degraded land have been identified for restoration. In coastal landscapes, the MISHTI initiative is advancing mangrove restoration while strengthening climate resilience and supporting local livelihoods. India also highlighted that the number of Ramsar Sites in the country has reached 101.

The country also showcased Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam – Plant4Mother, a whole-of-government and whole-of-society initiative under which more than 3.5 billion saplings have been planted. India emphasised that international cooperation must move beyond global commitments to support country-driven implementation, capacity development, technology transfer and measurable outcomes on the ground. It underlined the need for effective and sustainable financing, particularly for developing countries, and encouraged FAO to strengthen support for accessing climate, biodiversity and blended finance and for developing long-term restoration programmes.

India also called for stronger coherence between FAO’s forestry work, the Global Forest Goals and other forest-related international processes, along with enhanced South-South and triangular cooperation for sharing knowledge, best practices and scalable solutions. The country reaffirmed its commitment to working with FAO and Member States in shaping the proposed UN Decade for Afforestation and Reforestation in line with Sustainable Forest Management, 2027–2036, with the objective of building a coherent continuum from restoration of degraded ecosystems to resilient, productive and inclusive forest landscapes.

DoWR, RD & GR to implement Special Campaign 6 during 02-31 October, 2026

headline: India Energy Week 2027 Sets the Stage for Global Energy Dialogue in Kolkata
fullText:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas

India Energy Week 2027 Sets the Stage for Global Energy Dialogue in Kolkata

Hon’ble Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas Shri Hardeep Singh Puri alongwith Hon’ble Chief Minister of West Bengal Shri Suvendu Adhikari formally announce Kolkata as the host city for India Energy Week 2027

Kolkata to host India Energy Week 2027

IEW 2027 theme: “Unlocking Innovation. Securing Energy. Shaping Tomorrow.”

75,000+ energy professionals and 700+ international exhibitors expected

IEW 2027 will be held from 28–31 January 2027 at the New Town Convention Centre, Kolkata, India

28 SEP 2026 8:11PM by PIB Delhi

As India’s energy demand continues to grow amid a rapidly shifting global energy landscape, the technologies, partnerships and strategic choices shaping the future of energy will be at the forefront of India Energy Week (IEW) 2027.

Making its debut in Kolkata from 28–31 January 2027 under the theme “Unlocking Innovation. Securing Energy. Shaping Tomorrow,” the fifth edition of IEW will serve as the first major global energy conclave of the year, bringing together policymakers, energy leaders, technology innovators, investors and industry stakeholders from across the world to explore pathways to strengthen global energy security and advance sustainability.

Held under the patronage of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, India Energy Week has grown rapidly since its debut in Bengaluru in 2023, expanding in scale, international participation and the breadth of issues addressed. At the fourth edition in Goa in 2026, the event brought together 75,000+ energy professionals, 700+ exhibiting companies, participants from more than 120 countries and 6,500+ conference delegates, reflecting its preeminent position among global energy conclaves.

Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas Shri Hardeep Singh Puri along with Chief Minister of West Bengal Shri Suvendu Adhikari formally announced Kolkata as the host city for India Energy Week 2027. Shri Adhikari thanked Shri Puri and the Petroleum & Natural Gas Ministry for bringing IEW 2027 to West Bengal. Shri Adhikari said a successful IEW 2027 would help attract new investment, expand existing projects and create employment opportunities in West Bengal.

The evolution of India Energy Week has taken place alongside India’s increasing importance to the global energy system. As the world’s fastest-growing major economy, India’s energy demand is expanding rapidly, while the country continues to balance energy security and affordability with its transition towards cleaner energy systems. India’s energy choices therefore have implications well beyond its borders, making the country a centre of the global energy conversation.

IEW 2027 will build on this context, focusing on the technologies, innovations and partnerships required to ensure energy security, affordability and sustainability for the globe, especially countries in the global South. The event will provide a meaningful platform for stakeholders from across the hydrocarbon and wider energy value chain to explore opportunities to scale innovation, strengthen energy security, improve efficiency and accelerate technology-led progress.

With energy security, affordability, technology, investment and sustainability increasingly interconnected, IEW 2027 promises to catalyse global efforts to find practical solutions to the challenges shaping the sector. The exhibition and conference programmes will showcase developments across oil and gas, LNG, refining and petrochemicals, hydrogen, biofuels, digitalisation and AI, alongside other emerging areas within the energy sector.

Kolkata: A New Chapter for India Energy Week

The move to Kolkata brings India Energy Week to eastern India for the first time, adding a new geographical dimension by providing a platform for businesses, institutions and energy stakeholders from the region to engage with international partners and participate in global conversations on energy.

The fifth edition is expected to bring together 75,000+ energy professionals and 700+ international exhibitors, alongside the decision-makers in the energy domain. The exhibition and conference programmes will provide opportunities to showcase technologies, forge partnerships and explore the strategic opportunities and challenges shaping the energy sector.

The international character of India Energy Week has also grown alongside its scale. Previous editions have brought together senior government leaders and energy executives from major energy-producing and consuming economies. 17 Ministers and Deputy Ministers from countries including UAE, Canada, Netherlands, Oman, Brunei, Myanmar, Tanzania participated in IEW 2026, along with International organisations such as the International Energy Forum, BIMSTEC and the Eurasian Economic Union.

Their participation reflected the increasingly interconnected nature of the energy conversation, as countries and companies navigate questions around energy security, investment, technology, transition and the changing global energy landscape.

About India Energy Week

India Energy Week is the country’s flagship global energy platform, bringing together government leaders, industry executives and innovators to accelerate progress toward a secure, sustainable and affordable energy future. As a neutral platform, India Energy Week drives investment, policy alignment and technological collaboration shaping the global energy landscape.

Held under the patronage of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, India Energy Week 2027 is being organised by Federation of Indian Petroleum Industry (FIPI) with Informa Markets as Conference Organiser.

India Energy Week 2027 will take place from 28–31 January 2027 at the New Town Convention Centre, Kolkata, under the theme “Unlocking Innovation, Securing Energy, Shaping Tomorrow.”

For more information, visit: https://www.indiaenergyweek.com/

French Minister H.E. Mr Philippe Baptiste is on a three-day visit to India from September 28 to 30, 2026

Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi, held a bilateral meeting with Minister for Higher Education, Research and Space of France, H.E. Philippe Baptiste, in New Delhi today. The Ministers exchanged views on further promoting knowledge partnerships between the two countries and discussed opportunities to build upon existing institutional collaborations and create new avenues for joint academic and research initiatives. French Higher Educational Institutions were invited to explore opening of branch campuses in India including in GIFT City, Gujarat and also at places where French companies were located and required technical human resources.

Acknowledging the importance of people to people ties, the two sides explored opportunities to strengthen language learning and teacher education, share academic expertise and promote technology-enabled learning. The discussions also covered ongoing revision of the Mutual Recognition of Qualifications (MRQ) Agreement between India and France, sharing experiences and best practices in digital education and leveraging technology to expand access to quality learning.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurated the Conference on ‘PRAHAAR - CT Policy and Strategy’ today in New Delhi. The Conference deliberated upon the seven pillars of PRAHAAR including Prevention, Response, Aggregating Internal Capacities, Human Rights, Attenuating Conditions for Terrorism, Aligning International Efforts and Recovery &Resilience through a whole-of-society approach. The Conference was attended by Union Home Secretary, Foreign Secretary, Heads of CAPFs/CPOs, DGsP of 15 States, ATS Chiefs of all the States/UTs in person while other State DGsP and cutting-edge police officers joined the Conference virtually.

In his address, Union Home Minister said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India has adopted a 'zero-tolerance' policy against all forms and manifestations of terrorism.He also stressed on the need for consistent efforts to strengthen and improvise the PRAHAAR strategy through a continuous analysis of terror incidents and establishing a strong and concrete PRAHAAR mechanism for the next 10 years. Focussing on percolation of the tenets of PRAHAAR up to the Thana level, he impressed upon adopting a proactive approach towards every aspect of the PRAHAAR initiative. Mentioning various steps undertaken for mitigating terrorist threats, he advocated institutionalising an automated counter terrorism response at every level of the framework. Impressing upon the necessity of result-oriented approach towards each pillar of PRAHAAR, he called for coordination among the stakeholders to prevent any delay in action. headline: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Reviews Progress of Lady Hardinge Medical College and its Associated Hospitals
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Reviews Progress of Lady Hardinge Medical College and its Associated Hospitals

Shri Nadda Emphasises Long-Term Vision, Quality and Timely Execution for Upcoming Infrastructural Projects

Union Health Minister visits Advanced Simulation-Based Training and Neonatal Care Facilities at LHMC and KSCH; Highlights the role of simulation-based training and advanced neonatal care in strengthening patient safety and clinical outcomes

28 SEP 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda reviewed the progress of Lady Hardinge Medical College (LHMC) and its associated hospitals, Smt. Sucheta Kriplani Hospital (SSKH) and Kalawati Saran Children’s Hospital (KSCH), with a focus on strengthening healthcare infrastructure, specialised clinical services, medical education, research and patient care.

During the review meeting, the Minister was apprised of the ongoing augmentation of Kalawati Saran Children’s Hospital. The project envisages increasing the hospital’s total bed capacity from 394 to 894 beds, ICU capacity from 40 to 200 beds and the number of Operation Theatres from 4 to 12. Construction work on the KSCH campus is underway and is aimed at strengthening tertiary and super-speciality paediatric care, while also expanding capacity for undergraduate, postgraduate and super-speciality medical education and training.

Addressing the review meeting, Shri Nadda emphasised that the ongoing and upcoming projects at LHMC and its associated hospitals must be planned with a patient-centric and future-oriented approach, keeping evolving medical requirements at the core. He stressed that planning and design should draw upon the expertise and best practices of leading institutions in the relevant fields, while ensuring high quality of construction and strict monitoring of project timelines. He called for timely escalation of issues requiring approvals and clearances to the Ministry and emphasised that infrastructure expansion and recruitment of nurses, doctors and other healthcare professionals must progress concurrently.

Looking ahead, he called for a comprehensive master plan with a long-term institutional vision, combining immediate priorities with phased development and a forward-looking perspective for the coming decades. He also encouraged exploring private-sector expertise and partnerships, wherever appropriate, in planning and implementing major projects, while ensuring that quality, efficiency and patient care remain central to all such initiatives.

As part of the visit, the Union Health Minister visited the state-of-the-art Skill Lab at Lady Hardinge Medical College, a comprehensive multidisciplinary simulation-based training facility that provides hands-on and competency-based learning in a safe and controlled environment. The facility has dedicated simulation areas for ICU, surgical skills, simulated OT, Obstetrics OT, NICU, trauma, ENT and ophthalmology, along with briefing and debriefing areas and task trainers for procedural skills.

The Skill Lab provides an integrated platform for undergraduate and postgraduate training, procedural skills development, faculty development, multidisciplinary team training and competency-based assessment. Simulation-based learning, deliberate practice and structured feedback at the facility support the development of clinical and surgical proficiency, decision-making, teamwork, communication and crisis-resource management, while contributing to enhanced patient safety.

The Minister also visited the recently functional Augmented Level III-B Neonatal Care Centre at Kalawati Saran Children’s Hospital and reviewed the advanced facilities available for newborn care.

The Department of Neonatology has 80 intensive care beds and caters to more than 10,000 deliveries and 2,500 NICU admissions annually, with overall survival exceeding 93 per cent. The neonatal care facility provides advanced services including high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV), inhaled nitric oxide therapy, therapeutic hypothermia, advanced monitoring and comprehensive respiratory support.

The recently functional NICU-B comprises 7 NICU beds, 8 HDU beds, 15 Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) beds and 12 mothers’ cots, with emphasis on family-integrated care, kangaroo mother care and breastfeeding support.

The review and visit underscored the continued efforts of LHMC and its associated hospitals to strengthen advanced patient care, specialised paediatric and neonatal services, medical education, simulation-based training and research, alongside the ongoing expansion and modernisation of healthcare infrastructure.

District Awareness Programme on Labour Codes Held at Regional Labour Institute, Faridabad as part of Shram Samvad Initiative

28 SEP 2026 6:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Labour and Employment organised a District Awareness Programme, as part of its “Shram Samvad” Awareness Campaign, at the Regional Labour Institute, Faridabad today. The Shram Samvad Campaign, launched with effect from today, is aimed at creating awareness among stakeholders regarding the recently introduced Labour Codes and the key provisions and compliances applicable thereunder. Industrial clusters across 316 districts in all 36 States and Union Territories will be covered over the next 90 days under this initiative.

The programme at Faridabad witnessed enthusiastic participation from around 75 participants including employers, state authorities, advocates and other representatives and stakeholders from the labour and employment ecosystem. It was structured into five informative sessions, covering the major provisions of the new Labour Codes, employer compliances, and key social security schemes of the Government of India.

The inaugural address was given by Ms. Mridula Ghai, ACC, Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), and Ms. Aprajita Jaggi, ACC, EPFO. Mr. Ashish Wig, Member, Central Board of Trustees & Chair HR and IR Committee, PHDCCI, also addressed the gathering on this occasion.

The session focused on providing participants with a broad understanding of the Labour Codes and their significance for employees and employers.

The second session was conducted by Mr. Hemant Tirkey, Labour Welfare Commissioner, who elaborated upon the major compliances to be undertaken by employers under the Labour Codes. The session provided practical insights into the responsibilities and statutory requirements applicable to employers and helped participants understand the compliance framework under the new Codes.

The third session focused on the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Scheme and was conducted by Mr. Sunil Gautam, Assistant Welfare Commissioner. The participants were apprised of the salient features of the scheme and its role in extending social security benefits to eligible unorganised workers.

headline: NITI Aayog organises National Workshop on “Viksit Panchayat: Connecting People, Places, Resources and Opportunities”- an initiative under NITI Aayog’s State Support Mission (SSM)
fullText:
NITI Aayog organises National Workshop on “Viksit Panchayat: Connecting People, Places, Resources and Opportunities”- an initiative under NITI Aayog’s State Support Mission (SSM)

29 SEP 2026 5:40PM by PIB Delhi

NITI Aayog organised a national workshop on “Viksit Panchayat: Connecting People, Places, Resources and Opportunities” on 28th September 2026, in collaboration with the Golap Borbora State Institute of Panchayat & Rural Development (GBSIPRD), Government of Assam. The workshop focused on strengthening Panchayats as institutions capable of driving inclusive growth, effective public service delivery, and sustainable development at the grassroots, in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

The one-day National Workshop was inaugurated by Shri Atul Bora, Minister, Panchayat & Rural Development Department, Government of Assam, as the Chief Guest; Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, as the Guest of Honour; Dr. Ravi Kota, Chief Secretary, Government of Assam; and Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development.

The inaugural session highlighted the importance of decentralised governance, spatial planning, capacity development, digitalisation, and convergence for advancing Viksit Gram Panchayats. The deliberations focused on four key areas: decentralised and spatial planning, grassroots capacity development, spatial planning for priority sectors, and integration of spatial planning into the GPDP process.

Participants discussed the constitutional foundation of Panchayati Raj under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment and Part IX of the Constitution. Discussions also focused on clearer activity mapping, adequate financial resources, appropriate staffing, greater decision-making authority, Gram Sabha participation, and institutional accountability. The workshop emphasised the need to move from a sectoral to a spatial and integrated approach to local development. GIS, geospatial data, village master plans, and digital platforms were discussed for identifying local resources, infrastructure gaps, land-use patterns, and development opportunities. headline: When Swachhata Becomes Shared Faith
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

When Swachhata Becomes Shared Faith

From Ancient Traditions to Modern Pilgrimages, How Cleanliness Is Becoming a Collective Habit

29 SEP 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi

Swachhata in Ancient India: A Practice Rooted in Everyday Life

India’s association with cleanliness is older than the modern sanitation movement. The archaeological record of the Indus Valley reveals sophisticated sanitation systems. Cities like Lothal, in present-day Gujarat, followed planned layouts with extensive drainage networks. Many homes had private toilets connected to drains. The system also included inspection points and structures for managing solid waste. The Vedic tradition placed utmost importance on clean bodies and clean surroundings. Clean water, fresh air, and healthy surroundings were linked with spiritual practice. Ancient instructions also advised people to avoid defecating near rivers and other water bodies. The same connection appears in Buddhist traditions. Buddhist monks were instructed not to defecate or urinate in water. They were also expected to clean toilet areas for the next person. Archaeological findings support this tradition of organised sanitation. A Gupta-period monastery in Bihar had a dedicated toilet chamber.

These examples show an important idea. Swachhata has always been linked with conduct, discipline, and community life in India.

From Sanitation Infrastructure to Social Behaviour Change

Centuries later, however, sanitation has emerged as a challenge in modern-day India. This challenge is as much about having adequate sanitation systems as about building habits to ensure their use and sustained maintenance. The Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) was launched on 2 October 2014 to address this challenge. It became one of India’s largest government-led sanitation movements. The Mission has two components: Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen (SBM-G) and Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban (SBM-U). SBM-G focuses on rural sanitation, toilet access and usage, and solid and liquid waste management. SBM-U focuses on urban sanitation, waste management, public spaces, and cleanliness infrastructure.

On one hand, the decade since 2014 has seen construction of extensive sanitation infrastructure across the country - from toilets to waste disposal and management systems. On the other hand, this journey has tackled the much more difficult task of bringing about and sustaining behavioural change to make Swachhata part of routine behaviour. That is the larger transformation taking place under SBM.

While permanent villages and cities have now institutionalized waste management, this behavioral shift faces its ultimate test during massive religious gatherings, where millions assemble in compressed timeframes.

Maha Kumbh: A Massive Gathering Becomes a Swachhata Movement

Few gatherings demonstrate this transition as clearly as Maha Kumbh 2025. The scale itself presented a major sanitation challenge. Millions of devotees gathered at Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. The response to this challenge combined provision of adequate sanitation infrastructure with awareness generation and public participation. More than 28,000 toilets and 20,000 community urinals were established across the fairgrounds. The waste system included 20,000 trash bins for source segregation. But infrastructure was only one part of the story. The fairgrounds were designated as plastic-free zones. Awareness campaigns were organized to encourage devotees to avoid plastic waste. Public participation was actively encouraged in ensuring swachhata. A Swachhata Rath Yatra moved through Prayagraj. This was a public procession that promoted cleanliness and raised public awareness about avoiding littering, using dustbins, and refraining from using single-use plastic. Street plays and musical performances explained waste segregation and disposal. Public address systems carried cleanliness messages across the ghats.

The approach also created space for community-led action. Women from 28 districts of Uttar Pradesh, along with artisans from several neighbouring states, produced sustainable products. These products included leaf plates, kulhads, jute bags and cloth bags. Around 60 crore eco-friendly products were produced and sold at 300 locations. The message was not only about removing waste. It was about involving people in preventing waste. That is the essence of behaviour change.

Maha Kumbh 2025 also showed how robust public cleanliness systems can reinforce public behaviour. After major bathing dates, rapid sanitation teams restored the fairgrounds. They cleaned toilets and removed waste left behind by pilgrims. Disinfection and fogging were also undertaken.

Kanwar Yatra: When the Route Itself Becomes a Swachhata Space

If the river banks of Prayagraj tested massive demographic coordination, the linear routes of the Kanwar Yatra presented a different logistical puzzle. Millions of devotees travel along common routes during the pilgrimage. This creates pressure on roads, ghats, resting places and public facilities. In Delhi, a special cleanliness campaign was undertaken during the Yatra. Additional sanitation workers were deployed along major routes and resting points. Round-the-clock sweeping and waste collection were arranged. Temporary toilets were also provided. Special attention was given to wet and dry waste segregation. Single-use plastic was also discouraged. The campaign also addressed women pilgrims. Delhi introduced two special pink Kanwar camps for women managed by female volunteers. The camps included clean toilets and bathing facilities. This connected sanitation with dignity and convenience. More than 5 lakh devotees were also provided steel Ganga-water containers and jute bags as eco-friendly alternatives to plastic products.

Amarnath Yatra: From Faith to Responsible Action

Moving from dusty highways to the fragile ecosystem of the Kashmir Himalayas, the Amarnath Yatra elevates this responsibility further. More than four lakh pilgrims undertook the Yatra in 2025. The yatra has been aligned with SBM-U 2.0. The focus includes scientific waste management and plastic-free practices. The goal is a zero-landfill and eco-friendly Yatra. Swachhata Executives and other volunteers appointed by the state government supported the effort. They worked across lodgement centres, langar sites, and Yatra camps. They promoted segregation and discouraged single-use plastic. They also spread messages about sanitation and hygiene. The scale of operations was significant. Around 11.67 metric tonnes of waste were generated daily. Yet, 100% of this waste was processed. There were 1,016 twin-bin stations along the Yatra route for both wet and dry waste. Separate bins were placed near female toilets for sanitary waste. Around 1,300 SafaiMitras worked at strategic locations. They supported round-the-clock cleanliness along the route.

Awareness efforts were made interactive. Activities included ‘Plastic Lao, Thela Lejao’ and ‘Bin It, Win It’. These activities connected communication with participation. The IEC campaign also used signage and street plays. A Green Pledge campaign brought together more than 70,000 devotees. Participants committed themselves to Swachhata and sustainable practices. Social media reinforced the messageas pilgrims shared selfies and successful sanitation stories. Here, the change becomes especially visible.

Here, the pilgrim is no longer only a user of sanitation facilities. The pilgrim becomes a participant in maintaining them. Faith becomes connected with responsibility.

When Religious Practice Itself Becomes Part of Waste Management

The movement is also reaching religious spaces outside major pilgrimages. A striking example comes from Hyderabad. The Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation launched Project Udvasana. The project focuses on religious and sacred waste. Such material can include flowers, garlands, religious books, and damaged idols. The project provides dedicated collection and scientific processing. It began as a pilot at the ISKCON Temple in Jubilee Hills. Seven participants initially deposited 66 kilograms of religious material. The second phase collected 443 kilograms. The third phase expanded to six major temples. It involved 124 devotees. The collection reached 753.59 kilograms during this phase. The material was segregated, documented, and recycled. It was sent to an authorised agency for further processing. The initiative promotes source-level segregation and sustainable waste management. This is an important extension of the Swachhata journey. The focus is no longer only on cleaning public spaces. It is also on changing how religious waste is handled.

When Cleanliness Becomes Part of the Journey

India’s sanitation journey has travelled a long distance. Ancient settlements developed sophisticated systems for water and sanitation. Religious traditions connected cleanliness with personal and spiritual discipline. Modern India then faced the challenge of universal sanitation access. The Swachh Bharat Mission created a massive sanitation infrastructure. But infrastructure alone could not complete the journey. The next step was to make Swachhata a habit. That required communication, participation, and repeated public action. Today, that effort is visible beyond campaign days. It is visible on pilgrimage routes and at religious gatherings. It is visible in public spaces, temples, and festival sites. That is when Swachhata moves beyond a campaign. It becomes a habit, and when a habit becomes collective, it becomes a culture.

The Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign being observed from 17 September to 17 October 2026, carries the theme Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat.

The theme of the Shivir is Samman Safai Mitron Ka, Sankalp Swachh Bharat Ka. The Shivir aims to recognise and honour the vital contribution of SafaiMitras and facilitate their access to health, safety and social protection measures.

The Shivir will be organised in hybrid mode. The physical event will be held at Kedarnath Sahni Auditorium, Dr. S.P.M. Civic Centre, New Delhi while Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Rural Local Bodies (RLBs) and line departments from across the country will participate virtually.

headline: TDB signs agreement with Multi Nano Sense Technologies for ₹37.51 crore RDI support to build indigenous multi-gas sensing platform
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

TDB signs agreement with Multi Nano Sense Technologies for ₹37.51 crore RDI support to build indigenous multi-gas sensing platform

MEMS-based sensor and AFE SoC to advance from TRL-4 to TRL-9, strengthening India’s capabilities in advanced sensors and semiconductor technologies

29 SEP 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi

From industrial safety and hydrogen infrastructure to energy systems and process monitoring, the ability to detect and accurately measure gases is becoming increasingly important across a wide range of emerging technologies. Giving a boost to indigenous capabilities in this domain, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with M/s Multi Nano Sense Technologies Private Limited, Nagpur, Maharashtra for ₹37.51 crore financial support under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund. The project, with a total approved cost of ₹75.02 crore, focuses on the development of a Platform MEMS + AFE SoC Multi-Gas Sensor, with the objective of taking the technology from TRL-4 to TRL-9. The support will be provided through Optionally Convertible Debt (OCD).

Multi Nano Sense is developing an indigenous MEMS TCDIR gas sensor and CMOS AFE SoC platform aimed at enabling reliable and scalable multi-gas sensing in a compact form factor. The technology combines a MEMS-based sensing element with an application-specific front-end system-on-chip for signal acquisition and processing. The platform is designed for applications spanning leak detection, process control and health and safety monitoring, with potential use across industries including refineries, petrochemicals, power, PNG infrastructure, industrial safety, batteries and the hydrogen economy.

The proposed sensor platform is designed around a combination of high sensitivity, low power consumption, miniaturised and intelligent signal processing combination of MEMS Gas Sensor and a custom AFE SoC. The technology is intended to operate across a wide temperature range and in demanding industrial environments, while incorporating features such as auto-calibration, compensation for environmental parameters and software-based gas-library processing. With a targeted response time of less than 200 milliseconds, the platform is being developed for applications requiring rapid detection and monitoring. Its compact architecture, with a sensor package designed to be less than 25 mm × 25 mm × 15 mm, also opens possibilities for battery-operated and embedded applications.

The RDI-supported programme will enable Multi Nano Sense to undertake further development, integration, testing, validation and scale-up of the sensor and AFE SoC platform, with the ultimate objective of taking the technology to TRL-9. The project comes under the Deep Technology sector, with Quantum Technology identified as the sub-sector. While the immediate application is advanced multi-gas sensing, the underlying platform brings together MEMS, semiconductor electronics and intelligent sensing, areas that are increasingly important for building indigenous technology capabilities.

Sh. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said, “Sensors are the foundation of many modern technology systems, and indigenous capabilities in sensing and semiconductor technologies are important for both industrial competitiveness and strategic self-reliance. The RDI Fund enables us to support technologies that require sustained development before they can reach widespread commercial deployment. The agreement with Multi Nano Sense demonstrates how such support can help Indian deep-tech companies take advanced sensor technologies from development to scalable, market-ready solutions.”

Representative of Multi Nano Sense Technologies Private Limited said, “The RDI support from TDB will enable us to take our MEMS gas-sensing technology to the next stage of integration, validation and scale-up. Our objective is to develop a compact, low-power and scalable multi-gas sensing platform that can address demanding applications across industries. This support will be instrumental in advancing the technology towards TRL-9 and strengthening indigenous capabilities in MEMS and sensor electronics.”

- Announcement dated 29 September 2026, issued by PIB Delhi.

Continued medical care, family support and follow-up services can provide the encouragement needed to move towards recovery and a stable livelihood.

Bittu (name changed), a 28-year-old man from the OBC community in Banka, Bihar, was facing multiple socio-economic challenges that adversely affected his personal life, social relationships and overall opportunities for growth and development. Following treatment and rehabilitation support, Bittu has also demonstrated improvement in occupational functioning and income stability through his fruit-selling business. This progress has helped him move towards greater self-reliance while continuing his recovery journey.

Bittu's journey demonstrates how sustained rehabilitation, medical support, counselling and family guidance can help individuals navigate difficult circumstances and take meaningful steps towards recovery, stability and productive participation in society. headline: Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal Launches PRAGATI-50 initiative to Develop 50 Model Cities for Swachhata in New Delhi today
fullText:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs

Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal Launches PRAGATI-50 initiative to Develop 50 Model Cities for Swachhata in New Delhi today

Swachh Bharat Test Bed by CSIR-CMERI launched

3rd Cohort of Swachhata Startups onboarded in collaboration with IIT Kanpur

Reduce Reuse and Recycle Centre of Sankalp Bhawan, New Delhi inaugurated

Swachchata Behaviour Change Digital Kosh launched

29 SEP 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi

In pursuance to directions of the Hon’ble Prime Minister during the 51st PRAGATI meeting, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has identified 50 model cities under the PRAGATI-50 initiative for demonstrating a higher benchmark of ‘Swachhata’ through targeted, KPI-based action and by leveraging intensive and technology-enabled monitoring within the framework of Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban 2.0.

Click here to see the list of cities

Speaking at the launch, Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal emphasized: “These 50 cities across 24 states will emerge as clean role‑model cities for the rest of the country, by going beyond their routine sanitation work to demonstrate sustained, high-performance parameters of visible cleanliness. We have ensured inclusion of major cities, cities of cultural importance, high tourism destinations and economic centres. The initiative aims to drive visible improvements in urban cleanliness, solid waste management, used water management, sanitation, and citizen participation through a structured framework of monitoring and review within a defined timeframe. Progress will be continuously reviewed through outcome‑based assessments and tech‑enabled monitoring. I will personally chair review meetings every other month to track the advancement of these cities.”

In his remarks, Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu, said that over the past decade, Swachhata has evolved from a people’s movement into a way of life.

Referring to the launch of the new model cities initiative, Shri Sahu said that it would help cities achieve the goal of Garbage Free Cities within a stipulated timeframe and enable them to emerge as role models for other urban centres. He called upon States and Urban Local Bodies to prepare micro-level action plans and ensure their swift and effective implementation.

Highlighting the growing convergence of youth power and technology, the Minister noted that India has emerged as the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. He added that the launch of the third cohort in collaboration with IIT Kanpur also marks the achievement of the national target of onboarding and incubating 75 startups under the Mission.

The Secretary, Department of Urban Development (DoUD), MoHUA, Sh. Satendra Singh said that the efforts will be made towards ensuring better citizen experience and holistic service delivery. He highlighted that the initiative adopts “City as a Whole’” approach, ensuring all stakeholders, partners; Urban Local Bodies are included in the planning and implementation.

To ensure efficient monitoring, a Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation (PRAGATI) -like digital review mechanism has been established on the Swachhatam Portal. Officers from the Ministry will be assigned specific cities for regular supervision and handholding.

Recognizing that sustainable urban transformation hinges on building capacities and continuous learning, SBM‑U has empowered stakeholders with technical guidelines, model designs, and targeted advisories. During the programme, to further support the on-ground implementation of projects, Standard Operating Procedure for Establishment of Secondary Collection Centre for Construction & Demolition Waste (C&D) and Guidelines for Source Segregation of Municipal Solid Waste mandated under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 were released.

Swachh Bharat Test Bed & Innovation Centre : The Mission has consistently positioned research and innovation as the driving force of Swachhata. In collaboration with CSIR‑CMERI, MoHUA launched the Swachh Bharat Test Bed & Innovation Centre at Durgapur, a national facility for research, product development, testing, validation, certification, and capacity building in sanitation technologies.

The third cohort of startups : Over the past decade, SBM–Urban has shifted from conventional waste management to cutting-edge, tech-driven solutions. The Mission has engaged 75 startups across the waste value chain to accelerate innovation. Riding the wave of entrepreneurial momentum, MoHUA in collaboration with the Startup Incubation and Innovation Centre (SIIC) at IIT Kanpur, has launched the third cohort of startups focused on pioneering solutions in sanitation and waste management. With 13 startups joining Cohort 3, the initiative is fast-tracking cleaner, tech-driven urban solutions.

Dedicated WhatsApp channel : Taking the Swachhata App—an important interface for citizens to register complaints and seek grievance redressal—a step further, a dedicated WhatsApp channel has been launched to make it easier for citizens to lodge their complaints and actively contribute to keeping their cities clean.

The Swachhata Behaviour Change Digital Kosh- a digital repository bringing together Ideas, Creatives, Campaigns and Resources to strengthen behaviour change for a cleaner and more sustainable India was launched by Union Minister, Shri Manohar Lal. The platform will provide States, ULBs and stakeholders with ready-to-use communication resources, innovative campaign ideas and advocacy materials —enabling knowledge sharing, replication and citizen-centric communication to make Swachhata a habit and a way of life.

Reduce Reuse and Recycle (RRR): As part of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, Union Minister, Shri Manohar Lal inaugurated a Reduce Reuse and Recycle (RRR) Centre at Sankalp Bhawan, New Delhi. It envisaged as the first such centre in a Union Ministry office. The initiative will promote sustainable consumption, reuse, resource recovery and circularity in government workplaces.

A pivotal leap in India’s urban sanitation journey — MoHUA is driving innovation, peer learning, and capacity building to shape resilient, future‑ready cities. As India marches towards Viksit Bharat 2047, the path ahead is clear: garbage‑free cities powered by scientific waste management, circular economy, and sustainable urban systems.

fullText:
Ministry of Defence

India stands as the First Responder, Preferred Security Partner in the Indian Ocean Region: Shri Rajnath Singh

The Presence of Indian warships in South China Sea, Mediterranean, Atlantic Ocean, demonstrates India’s blue-water force capability

If the seas are secure, India will be secure; if India is secure, the resolve for a Viksit Bharat will be further strengthened: Raksha Mantri

Shri Rajnath Singh addresses the 2nd Indian Navy's Commanders' Conference

29 SEP 2026 3:47PM by PIB Delhi

“India stands firm as the First Responder, Preferred Security Partner and as a symbol of trust and reliability in the Indian Ocean Region and the entire world is witnessing the growth of both our strategic position and our strategic responsibility in the region. Today, issues such as congestion, deception, and gray-zone activities have made our maritime domain far more complex than ever before. Hence, we must elevate our monitoring and response mechanisms to a new level,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh while addressing the second edition of the Indian Navy's biannual Commanders' Conference 2026 at Nausena Bhawan, New Delhi, on September 29, 2026.

Raksha Mantri asserted that the presence of Indian warships extends to the South China Sea, the Mediterranean, and the Atlantic Ocean, demonstrating our blue-water force capability. The role of the Indian Navy is crucial in ensuring the strategic depth and regional power projection, he added.

Highlighting the government’s commitment to the modernization of the Navy under the leadership of the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri Rajnath stated, “The Indian Navy serves as a strategic anchor in the vision of 'Viksit Bharat 2047'. Beyond merely guarding maritime boundaries, our Navy strengthens economic protection, regional stability, and power projection.” He urged the Indian Navy to maintain its unrelenting momentum while transforming itself into a future-ready, combat-ready, and globally respected force.

Lauding the India Navy’s role in the crisis in West Asia, Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that ensuring the safe transit of Indian-flagged merchant vessels—particularly LPG tankers—through the Strait of Hormuz under ‘Operation Urja Suraksha’ is an outstanding achievement. India imports approximately 85–90 per cent of its crude oil and around 50 per cent of its natural gas through maritime routes; therefore, the security of sea lanes is directly connected with the country’s economy, energy supplies and defence preparedness, he added.

Underlining the Navy's efforts towards achieving self-reliance in the defence sector, Raksha Mantri emphasised, “The Indian Navy’s warship production ecosystem is now meeting global benchmarks. The warships commissioned recently contain over 75% indigenous content. In the times ahead, we must not only meet our own requirements but also export our warships to friendly foreign nations.

Shri Rajnath Singh called for a significant upgrade of India’s maritime surveillance architecture, recognising the importance of existing systems. He added that the growing volume and complexity of maritime traffic require enhanced analytical capabilities.

Shri Rajnath Singh described 2026 as a historic year for the Indian Navy, with plans for the induction or commissioning of 18 warships, which would constitute the largest single-year force accretion in the Navy’s history. “The developments reflected the growing maturity of India’s domestic naval shipbuilding ecosystem, while emphasising that further capability enhancement remained necessary,” he said.

Commending the Navy’s efforts towards women’s empowerment, recruitment and innovation under the “All Ranks, All Roles” approach, Raksha Mantri highlighted the deployment of women officers on frontline warships and aircraft. He also praised the participation of women in naval navigational expeditions, including the Navika Sagar Parikrama voyage.

Shri Rajnath Singh congratulated the Indian Navy on assuming command of Combined Task Force-154 under the Combined Maritime Forces, describing it as an important contribution to regional cooperative security. He also highlighted Operation Southern Readiness, conducted in Kochi during India’s command tenure of CTF-154, which involved 276 personnel from 27 countries, 76 facilitators and subject-matter experts, and four international organisations.

Raksha Mantri further commended the deployment of INS Sudarshini for Lokayan-26, which strengthened India’s maritime diplomacy and engagement with the Indian diaspora across the United States, Atlantic and Mediterranean regions while showcasing India’s maritime heritage.

Concluding his address, Shri Rajnath Singh commended the Indian Navy for maintaining a high level of combat readiness and fulfilling its commitments across the region despite evolving challenges. He said India’s maritime power is aimed not merely at displaying the national flag at sea, but at ensuring that wherever the Tricolour is seen, it conveys security, trust and confidence. He reaffirmed the Government’s support to the Indian Navy and said: “If the seas are secure, India will be secure; and if India is secure, the resolve for a Viksit Bharat will be further strengthened.”

Shri Rajnath Singh also interacted with the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) and the Chief of the Army Staff during the Conference. The three-day apex-level conference, being held from September 29, 2026 to October 01, 2026, brings together the top leadership of the Indian Navy to review operational preparedness, maritime security and future capability development.

headline: Government to Launch Special Campaign 6 from 2–31 October with Focus on Swachhata and Reducing Pendency
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

Government to Launch Special Campaign 6 from 2–31 October with Focus on Swachhata and Reducing Pendency

29 SEP 2026 3:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India will undertake Special Campaign 6 from 2 October to 31 October 2026, with emphasis on Swachhata (cleanliness) and reduction of pendency in government activities. The campaign will also focus on effective management of records, efficient utilisation of office space and scientific disposal of e-waste generated in government offices.

The annual campaign aims to institutionalise cleanliness practices in government offices and ensure time-bound disposal of pending references. A key area of emphasis during Special Campaign 6 will be the effective collection, segregation and scientific disposal of e-waste.

The campaign is being undertaken in three phases. During the Preparatory Phase from 15 to 30 September 2026, departments are identifying targets for disposal, including pending references from Members of Parliament, State Governments, inter-ministerial references, including Cabinet Notes, references from the PMO, Parliamentary Assurances pending for more than three months, Public Grievances and Appeals. The preparatory phase also includes review of files and records, recording and weeding of files, closure of e-files and identification of scrap and other redundant materials for disposal.

During the Implementation Phase from 2 to 31 October 2026, offices under the Department will undertake cleanliness activities, ensure scientific disposal of e-waste and other redundant materials, and take time-bound action for disposal of pending references.

The Evaluation Phase from 16 to 30 November 2026 will involve assessment and review of the work undertaken and outcomes achieved across Ministries and Departments.

Special Campaign 6 will place particular emphasis on effective collection, segregation and scientific disposal of e-waste generated in government offices. The Department is undertaking preparatory measures to ensure systematic management and environmentally responsible disposal of e-waste during the implementation phase.

During Special Campaign 5, the Department of Commerce comprehensively reviewed 88,385 physical files and weeded out 46,255 physical files. The exercise resulted in freeing up 36,005 sq. ft. of office space through systematic review and record management.

The Department also generated approximately Rs. 70 lakh through disposal of scrap and other redundant materials, while 277 sites were cleaned during the campaign.

Special Campaign 5 strengthened cleanliness, systematic record management, efficient utilisation of office space and responsible disposal of redundant materials across the offices of the Department of Commerce. Special Campaign 6 builds on these efforts with continued emphasis on cleanliness, reduction of pendency, record management, scientific e-waste disposal and efficient utilisation of government office space.

headline: DDWS organises Eleventh Edition of Sujal Gram Samvad
fullText:
Ministry of Jal Shakti

DDWS organises Eleventh Edition of Sujal Gram Samvad

Community Participation, Local Ownership and O&M of Rural Water Supply Assets Emphasised at the Multilingual dialogue

29 SEP 2026 2:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, organised the 11th edition of the multilingual ‘Sujal Gram Samvad’ today, providing a platform for direct interaction with Gram Panchayat representatives and local communities on operation and maintenance of rural drinking water systems. This reinforces the government’s commitment to community-led water governance under the Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.

The Samvad was chaired by Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, in the presence of Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM, along with Senior officers from the department.

In his opening address, Secretary, DDWS, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, underscored the critical role of Gram Panchayats in ensuring the sustainability and long-term functionality of rural drinking water systems. Describing Sujal Gram Samvad as an important platform for sharing innovations and good practices from the grassroots, he encouraged GPs to learn from each other's experiences and strengthen local water governance. He highlighted that the active participation of elected representatives, Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSCs) and local communities is essential for delivering regular, safe and reliable drinking water services to every household.

Emphasising the constitutional mandate of Panchayati Raj Institutions in the drinking water sector, Shri Meena stressed the need for greater ownership of operation and maintenance (O&M) by GPs. He called for strengthening user-charge collection mechanisms, improving financial sustainability of water supply schemes and undertaking source sustainability measures such as groundwater recharge and rainwater harvesting. He urged to effectively leverage State O&M policies and available resources to ensure sustainable service delivery and community ownership of drinking water infrastructure.

The 11th edition of Samvad featured grassroots interactions across 4 Gram Panchayat (GP) headquartered villages. The virtual Samvad witnessed a diverse range of participants including Gram Panchayat (GP) representatives, members of VWSCs, community participants, Jal Sahiyas, Anganwadi workers, students, teachers, and frontline functionaries from the GPs, along with JJM State Mission Directors, District Collectors/District Magistrates/Deputy Commissioners, DWSM officials, and senior officers from the States. The multilingual Samvad focused on key aspects of sustainable rural water service delivery, including uninterrupted operation of water supply schemes, skilling of local operators, water quality and disinfection, community participation in O&M, financial sustainability through user charges and convergence, protection of drinking water sources, Jal Arpan and the wider impact of reliable drinking water services on health, education, women’s empowerment and local livelihoods.

Voices from the Gram Panchayats

GP: Sakaria, District: Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh

During the interaction, representatives of GP Sakaria shared in Hindi that prior to Mission, villagers largely depended on wells and tube wells for drinking water. Today, every household in the village has access to piped drinking water and the village has achieved Har Ghar Jal status. The community informed that Jal Arpan was organised on 16 March 2026 and that drinking water services are being supported through regular collection of ₹150 per month as user charges, with payments and billing undertaken through digital platforms. Water quality is being monitored regularly, by weekly water quality testing, and trained local operators are supporting smooth operation of the scheme.

District and State officials emphasised the importance of sustaining service delivery in Har Ghar Jal villages through strong operation and maintenance systems, source sustainability measures and effective utilisation of available resources. Referring to the State O&M framework, AS&MD, NJJM asked to encourage Gram Panchayats to leverage the e-Gram Swaraj portal for planning and monitoring expenditure and to make effective use of 16th Finance Commission tied grants for strengthening drinking water infrastructure, source protection and long-term sustainability of water supply systems.

GP: Dashinpara, District: Alipurduar, West Bengal

During the interaction the GP representatives and community interacted in Nepali and said that shared that prior to Jal Jeevan Mission, the village faced significant challenges in accessing safe drinking water and depended largely on standposts and nearby wells. The Village Pradhan informed that today tap water reaches every household, school and Anganwadi centre, resulting in significant improvements in convenience, health and overall quality of life. Aangan Wadi Wotrker highlighted that the availability of safe drinking water has contributed to a reduction in water-borne illnesses and reduced the burden of fetching water. They also shared that safe drinking water is supporting nutrition, meal preparation and awareness activities among adolescent girls, pregnant women and lactating mothers. The Village Pradhan highlighted the role of the Pani Samiti in water quality monitoring, community mobilisation and awareness generation, with active participation of women.

District and State officials appreciated the strong community ownership demonstrated by the Gram Panchayat and noted that preparations are underway for Jal Arpan, which will further strengthen local ownership and long-term sustainability of rural drinking water assets.

GP: Gorabali South, District: Bokaro, Jharkhand

During the interaction with village representatives in Hindi, they highlighted the transformational impact of Jal Jeevan Mission on drinking water access and quality of life. They shared that household tap connections have significantly reduced hardship for rural families and improved access to safe drinking water. Particular emphasis was placed on the success of the Jal Sahiya model, through which women are playing a leading role in community mobilisation, user-charge collection, grievance redressal and awareness generation. The Panchayat informed that regular user charges are being collected and utilised locally for operation and maintenance of drinking water systems. Community representatives also highlighted water quality testing through FTKs, active Gram Sabha discussions and efforts to strengthen source sustainability.

District officials informed that around 15 successful community-led models, including the Jal Sahiya model, are currently operational across the district. They also highlighted innovative outreach initiatives such as Jal Samvad, under which officials directly visit Gram Panchayats and interact with local communities, and “Hamare Gaon Hamare Log”, organised every Saturday to engage with villagers on water supply services, community participation and planning for utilisation of 16th Finance Commission tied grants.

During the interaction, AS&MD,NJJM suggested that States prepare simplified O&M Manuals in local languages to enable Gram Panchayat representatives and VWSC members to better understand their responsibilities in managing rural water supply systems.

GP: Partapur, District: Nubra, Ladakh

During the interaction, village representatives shared in Hindi, that before Jal Jeevan Mission, accessing drinking water during harsh winter months was extremely difficult and often required villagers to travel to distant sources or use melted snow. Following the provision of household tap connections, drinking water is now available at homes throughout the year. Community members highlighted that water supply continues even during winter when temperatures fall to nearly minus 30 degrees Celsius, owing to appropriate engineering measures adopted in the water supply infrastructure. Students, teachers and villagers also confirmed the availability of safe drinking water facilities in schools and public institutions and highlighted growing awareness regarding water conservation and water quality monitoring.

State officials informed that efforts are underway to further strengthen drinking water infrastructure through improvement of headworks, source sustainability measures and implementation of the recently notified O&M Policy. They also highlighted ongoing planning for additional household tap connections, preparation of DPRs related to source sustainability and infrastructure strengthening, and continued focus on ensuring reliable water services in the challenging terrain and climatic conditions of Ladakh.

AS & MD, NJJM, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, emphasised that the long-term success of JJM 2.0 will depend on robust operation and maintenance systems, regular user-charge collection, source sustainability measures and active involvement of Panchayats and communities in managing drinking water assets.

Shri Soan highlighted the importance of utilising the 2 October Gram Sabha as a platform for promoting water conservation, drinking water security, sanitation and community awareness. He encouraged Gram Panchayats that have completed the Har Ghar Jal certification process to organise Jal Arpan programmes and suggested that States develop and disseminate O&M Manuals in local languages so that Panchayat representatives and VWSC members can more effectively manage and sustain rural water supply systems.

headline: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Calls for ‘Team Agriculture’ to Make India a Global Food Basket
fullText:
Ministry of Agriculture &

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Calls for ‘Team Agriculture’ to Make India a Global Food Basket

Centre, States Must Rise Above Politics to Put Farmers First: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

India’s Farm Produce Set to Gain Global Reach Through New Trade Opportunities: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

More than ₹1200 Crore PM-RKVY Support Sanctioned to 10 States at National Agriculture Conference

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Announces Stronger Centre-State Coordination and Nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’

Natural Farming, Integrated Agriculture and Crop Diversification Key to a More Sustainable Farm Sector: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

29 SEP 2026 2:15PM by PIB Delhi

On the second day of the National Agriculture Conference – Rabi Campaign 2026, Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan chaired a session attended by Agriculture Ministers and senior officials from various states. Addressing the gathering, Shri Chouhan said that under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Centre and states must rise above party politics and work in the spirit of ‘Team Agriculture’ to ensure the country’s food security and improve farmers’ livelihoods. “Governments and political parties come and go; parties are formed and dissolved, but the country and its farmers are eternal,” he said, stressing that the platform was not about politics but about finding practical ways to improve agriculture and advance the interests of farmers. Shri Chouhan also highlighted that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, farmers’ interests have been accorded the highest priority in every major policy decision and international agreement. At the conference, Shri Chouhan handed over financial sanction letters worth more than ₹1200 crore to Agriculture Ministers of 10 states under the Prime Minister Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY). Union Ministers of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shri Ram Nath Thakur and Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, Agriculture Secretary Shri Atish Chandra, ICAR Director General Dr. M. L. Jat, along with senior officials from the Centre and states, scientists and representatives of various agricultural institutions, were present at the conference.

More than ₹ 1200 crore sanctioned to 10 states under PM-RKVY

Under PM-RKVY, sanction letters were distributed to 10 states, including ₹290 crore for West Bengal, ₹198 crore for Haryana, ₹181 crore for Chhattisgarh, ₹154 crore for Arunachal Pradesh, ₹114 crore for Bihar, ₹104 crore for Karnataka, ₹75 crore for Mizoram, ₹64 crore for Himachal Pradesh, ₹58 crore for Jharkhand and ₹43 crore for Punjab.

Shri Chouhan said the Union Government was not limiting itself to policy formulation, but was also ensuring timely availability of resources to states so that implementation of schemes could begin on the ground without delay.

Agriculture growth rate rises to 4.5 per cent

Highlighting the country’s agricultural performance, Shri Chouhan said that since 2015, the agriculture growth rate has increased from 3 per cent to 4.5 per cent. The average annual increase in foodgrain production has also more than doubled, rising from around 40 lakh tonnes earlier to 84 lakh tonnes per year. He further noted that in just two years, from 2023-24 to 2025-26, rabi foodgrain production recorded an unprecedented increase of 205 lakh tonnes. He attributed this historic growth to the collective efforts of state agriculture departments, scientists and farmers.

Monthly virtual reviews with states to strengthen cooperative federalism

Announcing a new mechanism to further strengthen cooperative federalism, Shri Chouhan said that, on the lines of weekly reviews conducted at the Centre, regular monthly virtual review meetings with states would now be held to continuously assess progress. At the state level, a strong State Agriculture Team will be constituted by bringing together the Agriculture Minister, Agriculture Secretary, state agricultural universities, ICAR institutions, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), ATMA, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), progressive farmers, processors, exporters and nodal officers of the Government of India. At the district level, monthly meetings will be held involving the Collector, Deputy Director of Agriculture (DDA), ATMA, KVKs, ICAR scientists, bankers and farmers.

Annual calendar for pre-season agriculture interface meetings

To ensure advance preparation for agricultural campaigns, Shri Chouhan announced an annual calendar for interface meetings. For the Kharif campaign, district-level meetings will be held on May 10 and state-level meetings on May 17 every year. Similarly, for the Rabi campaign, district-level meetings will be held on September 10 and state-level meetings on September 17 every year. In addition, a one-day special meeting will be organised across the country on a common date, bringing together Agriculture Ministers, officials and agricultural scientists simultaneously to discuss issues concerning farmers.

‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ from October 22 to November 30

Emphasising the need to protect soil health and the environment, Shri Chouhan called for a nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ from October 22 to November 30 this year. Scientists and all key stakeholders will actively participate in the campaign. Based on Soil Health Cards, the campaign will promote balanced use of fertilisers to protect soil fertility and beneficial insects. He also called for large-scale promotion of pulse cultivation in rice fallow areas of eastern India, particularly in Jharkhand, Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal, after the paddy harvest.

Rabi preparations to focus on soil moisture, water availability and crop protection

As part of preparations for the current rabi season, Shri Chouhan stressed that recommendations on crops and improved seeds should be based on soil moisture and water availability. He directed states to put in place effective arrangements to protect crops from diseases and pests, ensure saturation of all eligible farmers with Kisan Credit Cards (KCCs) and conduct transparent Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) under the crop insurance scheme. He also emphasised that state ministers should personally undertake regular reviews of the implementation of departmental schemes.

Strict action against spurious inputs, end to forced tagging

Stating that the availability of seeds and fertilisers in the country is adequate, Shri Chouhan directed states to take strict legal action against fake fertilisers, spurious seeds and sub-standard pesticides. He also directed that forced tagging be completely eliminated. Calling for agriculture to become more sustainable and remunerative, he urged states to adopt natural farming, integrated farming systems and crop diversification in mission mode.

Government working on multi-pronged strategy to ensure remunerative prices for farmers

Shri Chouhan said the government is pursuing a multi-dimensional strategy to ensure that farmers receive fair and remunerative prices for their produce. The strategy includes strengthening post-harvest management, scientific warehousing and marketing systems. He said that 100 per cent assured government procurement of tur, urad and masoor at MSP would be undertaken, with arrangements for payment within 48 hours. In line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision, he said India would also leverage the new market opportunities emerging from international Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) to connect Indian agricultural products, fruits, vegetables and foodgrains with global markets. This, he said, would help farmers secure better returns for their produce and enable India to emerge as a major ‘food basket’ for the world.

headline: Ministry of MSME and Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation Sign Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for development and strengthening of the Statistical Business Register
