Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises

Ministry of MSME and Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation Sign Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for development and strengthening of the Statistical Business Register

MoU will facilitate structured framework for sharing relevant information from Udyam Registration ecosystem

29 SEP 2026 1:33PM by PIB Delhi

A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) has been exchanged between Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), to institutionalize a mechanism for sharing relevant data for the development and strengthening of the Statistical Business Register (SBR).

The MoU was signed by Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME and Dr. Dalip Singh, Additional Director General, MoSPI, in the presence of senior officers from Ministry of MSME and MoSPI.

Objectives of the MoU:-

-The MoU sets the terms and understanding between the Ministry of MSME and MoSPI in relation to the sharing of unit-wise data of the Udyam Registration available with MSME Department through APIs. The two-way API shall provide data for preparation of National Statistical Business Register (NSBR).

-The MoU will facilitate a structured framework for sharing relevant information from the Udyam Registration ecosystem of the Ministry of MSME with MoSPI. The information will contribute to improving the coverage, consistency and reliability of business information used for statistical purposes.

Statistical Business Register (SBR): An Overview

-The Statistical Business Register (SBR) is a central and regularly updated database of registered statistical units engaged in economic activities within a defined geographical territory.

It captures businesses, enterprises, establishments & other relevant economic units, key characteristics of economic units and relationships between different units.

- The SBR serves as foundational infrastructure for the economic statistics system to improve the coverage, consistency and reliability of business information by identifying the target population for economic surveys, supporting survey sample selection, enabling the production of business demography statistics, providing a common framework for business demography-related information, and facilitating integration and consistency across different data sources.

headline: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to Undertake Special Campaign 6.0 with Focus on Cleanliness of National Highways and Toll Plazas

Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to Undertake Special Campaign 6.0 with Focus on Cleanliness of National Highways and Toll Plazas

29 SEP 2026 1:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) will undertake Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October 2026, with a special focus on improving cleanliness and upkeep of National Highways (NHs) and Toll Plazas. The campaign will also focus on reducing pendency, strengthening record management, promoting responsible disposal of e-waste and ensuring optimum utilisation of office space across organisations under the administrative control of the Ministry.

The campaign is being implemented in two phases. The Preparatory Phase, being undertaken from 15th to 30th September 2026, focuses on identification of targets and preparatory activities for cleanliness drives, disposal of obsolete items and other activities to be undertaken during the main campaign period commencing from 2nd October 2026.

Under Special Campaign 6.0, focused efforts will be undertaken for garbage removal along National Highways, particularly in urban areas; refurbishment of toilet blocks at Toll Plazas and other locations along NHs; cleaning and maintenance of functional toilets; and overall improvement in the upkeep of Toll Plazas. The campaign will also cover cleaning, painting, improved lighting and solarisation of Toll Plazas, installation and improvement of road signage, enhancement of visibility of road markings, and making National Highways pothole-free, among other activities.

As part of the campaign, the Ministry has identified a 50-km stretch of National Highway, including one Toll Plaza, for focused intervention. Officers from the Headquarters will be deputed to inspect the identified stretches and assess the impact of the cleanliness and improvement measures. The nominated officers will visit the assigned stretches, identify and geo-tag deficiencies, and continuously monitor the progress of rectification works. They will also ensure timely resolution of the identified deficiencies and improvement in cleanliness, safety and overall upkeep of the National Highway during the campaign period.

The Ministry has sensitised all Campaign Offices, including Headquarters, Regional Offices, Programme Implementation Units, Programme Directors and other field offices, to undertake concerted efforts for effective implementation of Special Campaign 6.0 and ensure visible and sustainable outcomes.

Nodal Officers have been nominated for organisations under the administrative control of the Ministry to coordinate and oversee implementation of the campaign within their respective organisations and regularly report progress to the Ministry. The Joint Secretary (Coord.) has been nominated as the Nodal Officer for overall coordination of Special Campaign 6.0 across the Ministry and its organisations.

The progress of Special Campaign 6.0 is being regularly reviewed by the Joint Secretary (Coord.) with the Nodal Officers of the Campaign Offices. The Secretary, MoRTH, is also regularly reviewing the progress of the Preparatory Phase during the weekly Senior Officers’ Meetings.

Through Special Campaign 6.0, the Ministry is endeavouring to ensure cleaner, safer and better-maintained National Highways and Toll Plazas, while strengthening efficiency, record management and workplace practices across its organisations.

headline: Ministry of Tribal Affairs and IGNCA Sign MoU for Preservation, Documentation and Promotion of Tribal Cultural Heritage
fullText:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs

Ministry of Tribal Affairs and IGNCA Sign MoU for Preservation, Documentation and Promotion of Tribal Cultural Heritage

Partnership to strengthen documentation, research, preservation and dissemination of India’s tribal cultural traditions

29 SEP 2026 1:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), an autonomous trust under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on September 28, 2026, for the preservation, documentation, digitisation, research and promotion of India’s diverse tribal cultural heritage.

The MoU was signed in New Delhi in the presence of Ms. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, and other senior officials of the Ministry. Dr. K. Anil Kumar, HoD, IGNCA, and other senior officials of IGNCA were also present on the occasion. The partnership brings together the Ministry’s tribal research ecosystem and network of Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) with IGNCA’s academic, archival, research and curatorial expertise.

The MoU aims to establish an institutional framework for collaboration between MoTA and IGNCA for the systematic preservation, documentation, digitisation, research and promotion of India’s diverse tribal tangible and intangible cultural heritage. It seeks to leverage the expertise and resources of both institutions to document, protect and disseminate tribal arts, music, languages, oral traditions, folklore, crafts, customary practices and traditional knowledge, while creating wider platforms for their recognition and promotion.

Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, appreciated the initiative to preserve and promote India’s rich tribal cultural heritage, and underlined the importance and significance of the collaboration. She highlighted that the partnership would contribute significantly to tribal empowerment and the wider promotion and recognition of India’s diverse tribal cultural traditions.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Ganesh Nagarajan, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, said, “This MoU provides an important institutional framework for bringing together the strengths of MoTA and IGNCA to preserve and promote India’s rich and diverse tribal cultural heritage.”

India’s tribal communities have a rich diversity of arts, music, musical instruments, crafts, cuisines, languages, oral traditions, folklore, customary practices and traditional ecological knowledge. Much of this heritage is living and community-based. The collaboration will provide an institutional framework for the systematic identification, documentation, digitisation, publication and dissemination of vanishing tribal arts, music, musical instruments, tribal cuisines and other cultural traditions.

The partnership will also support the identification, protection and promotion of endangered tribal languages, oral traditions, indigenous art forms and folklore. Another key area of cooperation will be the development of dedicated galleries and digital museums showcasing tribal arts, artefacts and the historical contributions of tribal communities to India’s freedom struggle. Youth camps in educational institutions and other centres of learning will be supported to promote awareness of tribal cultural values, sustainable conservation practices and the diversity of tribal customary practices and culture.

Dr. K. Anil Kumar, HoD, IGNCA, said, “this is a crucial collaboration between MoTA and IGNCA to preserve, document, and promote India's rich and diverse tribal tangible and intangible cultural heritage. The partnership will also support establishment of digital archives, and designing state-of-the-art interactive tribal museum galleries including dedicated showcases highlighting the contributions of tribal communities to India’s freedom struggle.”

The collaboration will facilitate wider dissemination of tribal cultural heritage through exhibitions, museums, publications, digital platforms, cultural festivals and knowledge-sharing initiatives, while creating greater visibility for tribal scholars, artists, artisans, performers and traditional knowledge holders at national and international platforms.
